newsitem.title: USA: Sony to launch Web TV terminal next month.
newsitem.headline: Sony to launch Web TV terminal next month.

text.p: Sony Electronics Inc Monday said it would begin selling a unit next month that enables customers to use their television sets to gain access to the Internet.
The Sony Web TV Internet Terminal, model INT-W100, will be sold in U.S. consumer electronic stores at a suggested retail price of $349.
The company said it moved up the launch date because initial dealer response to the product has been so positive.

The unit is designed to sit on or near a television, connecting the set and a telephone line. It enables a customer to gain access to the World Wide Web within about 15 minutes of opening the box, the company said.
It will provide access to the World Wide Web through a subscription service offered by WebTV Networks Inc of Palo Alto, Calif.

The terminal will come with a remote control device that is compatible with all major television brands, as well as a 25-foot telephone cord and a phone-line splitter. It also will come with an A/C connection cable and an S-Video cable.

"We're taking the guesswork out of navigating the Web," said John Briesch, president of the company's consumer audio video group. "Now even without a computer, and without any computer knowledge or experience, people can enjoy the benefits of interactive on-line communication right from their televisions."
